summary: The exact candidate adds a coherent opt-in global timer read and caller-owned timestamp store. The missing API was reproduced on the prepared base, then passed on the candidate on a real gfx950 GPU. Candidate regressions, separate ISA inspection, exact numerical checks, overhead measurement, and an independent uneven-work adversarial kernel all passed. No candidate source was modified.

tests.what_was_measured: On base acf7e67b7d22847e345938ca54fcc137bd7b2a1f, real kernel lowering failed with AttributeError because flydsl.expr.rocdl.global_timer did not exist, reproducing the missing original capability.
At candidate 4f72a59a0306801071fee7ef2850c110d893ff33, the identical probe compiled, executed on GPU, and returned a nonzero uint64 timestamp.

Candidate-focused suite: 4 passed, 2 optional-backend tests skipped. The profiled vector add exactly matched the independent Torch a+b reference; stage intervals were positive (104/128/140 ticks min/median/max). Median HIP-event launch time was 37.640 us plain and 37.716 us profiled, delta 0.076 us and ratio 1.002x.

tests.command: Separate profiled/plain pytest invocations with FLYDSL_RUNTIME_ENABLE_CACHE=0, FLYDSL_DUMP_IR=1, and distinct dump directories, followed by rg -n 's_memrealtime|global_store_dwordx2|s_barrier' over each final ISA
tests.what_was_measured: The instrumented gfx950 ISA contains exactly two s_memrealtime reads, two global_store_dwordx2 timestamp stores, and one s_barrier. The uninstrumented specialization contains none of those instructions. Both numerical tests passed.

Independent uneven-work GPU kernel: exact integer results [4096, 8192, 12288, 16384], caller-layout guard sentinels preserved, and increasing measured intervals [7172, 13224, 20752, 27104] raw ticks for 1x through 4x global-load work.

gpu_evidence: One assigned AMD Instinct MI350X, gfx950:sramecc+:xnack-, executed the candidate regressions and independent adversarial kernel under Torch 2.9.1+rocm7.2.0.git7e1940d4 and HIP 7.2.26015-fc0010cf6a.
remaining_limitations: The candidate changes no C++ or LLVM source, so the prepared native rebuild command was not applicable. Checkout Python sources were confirmed active, and the native MLIR extension continued to resolve through /job/repo/python/flydsl/_mlir/_mlir_libs to the prepared pinned wheel build.
Only gfx950 was available. Other supported AMDGPU architectures were not executed in this review.

The s_memrealtime primitive supplies a same-device global time domain suitable for comparing workgroups across XCDs, but this environment provided no supported mechanism to identify or pin tested workgroups to distinct XCDs; actual cross-XCD placement was therefore not independently demonstrated.

Different GPUs do not have a guaranteed synchronized epoch. Timer reads do not establish stream ordering or memory/execution completion; callers must add the synchronization or waits appropriate to the stage. Raw ticks should not be converted to time without an independently established timer frequency.
